subject: Literature
title: Homer's Iliad and the Birth of Western Poetry
description: One-minute skill: Homer's Iliad and the Birth of Western Poetry.

hook.text: The Iliad begins not with a battle but with a personal argument between a king and his greatest warrior.

buildup.text: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War was composed orally around 750 BC and memorized for generations.

discovery.text: The poem does not celebrate war but mourns it, ending with the funeral of Hector, Troy's fallen defender.

twist.text: Scholars still debate whether Homer was one person, two, or a collective name for many oral poets.

climax.text: The Iliad created the template for Western narrative: conflict, character, consequence, and the cost of glory.

punchline.text: Western literature began with a poem mourning war's cost.

quiz.question: How does the Iliad treat war?
options: It glorifies battle as humanity's highest achievement
It mourns war and ends with the funeral of a fallen defender
It ignores combat and focuses on romance
